mekayis.metin:
(قَتَدَ) الْقَافُ وَالتَّاءُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ صَحِيحٌ، وَهُوَ كَلِمَتَانِ: الْقَتَدُ: خَشَبُ الرَّحْلِ، وَجَمْعُهُ أَقْتَادٌ وَقُتُودٌ. وَالْكَلِمَةُ الْأُخْرَى الْقَتَادُ: ضَرْبٌ مِنَ الْعِضَاهِ
لَيْسَ فِيهِ غَيْرُ هَذَا. وَيَقُولُونَ: قَتَائِدُ: مَكَانٌ.

vikisozluk_etimolojiler.metin: Regressively assimilated respectively progressively dissimilated in voicedness from dialectal variants قَدَاد (qadād), قَتَات (qatāt), also قَدِيد (qadīd), قَتِيت (qatīt), from قَدَّ (qadda), قَتَّ (qatta, “to snithe into strips, to cut lengthwise”) – the former more known, the latter however reflected in قَتّ (qatt, “lucerne”) and قَات (qāt, “qat”) –, as cutting, slitting is what one does with the milk-vetches, whose profusion of sap was also the motive for the derivation of كَثِيرَاء (kaṯīrāʔ, “tragacanth, gum of milk-vetches”).
See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.
